have a rare adrenal gland tumor called pheochromocytoma.

kidney or liver problems
seizures or an abnormal brain wave test (EEG)
circulation problems in the fingers or toes

Also tell your doctor if you are pregnant, intending to become pregnant, or breastfeeding.

Do not take Adderall if you or your child:
are allergic to amphetamine products or any of the ingredients in Adderall (see ingredients below)
are taking, or have taken within the past 14 days, an MAO inhibitor, including the antibiotic linezolid or the intravenous medicine methylene blue.
have a rare adrenal gland tumor called pheochromocytoma.
Before taking Adderall, tell your healthcare provider about all your medical conditions including if you or anyone in your family has ever had:
heart problems, heart disease, heart defects, or high blood pressure, or a family history of sudden death or heart problems
mental problems including psychosis, mania, bipolar illness, or depression, or a family history of suicide, bipolar illness, or depression
kidney or liver problems
seizures or an abnormal brain wave test (EEG)
circulation problems in the fingers or toes
repeated movements or sounds (tics) or Tourette's syndrome, or a family history of tics or Tourette's syndrome.
Also tell your doctor if you are pregnant, intending to become pregnant, or breastfeeding.

Call your healthcare provider right away if you or your child have any new or worsening mental symptoms during treatment.

It is also important if you see or believe things that are not real.
It is also important if you have new manic symptoms.
Circulation problems:
You may have blood circulation problems that can cause numbness, pain, or discoloration in your fingers or toes.
Call your doctor right away if you have unexplained wounds appearing on your fingers or toes during treatment.
Other warnings:
Do not use Adderall if you have used an MAO inhibitor in the past 14 days.
Examples of MAO inhibitors include isocarboxazid, linezolid, phenelzine, rasagiline, selegiline, or tranylcypromine.
Do not use Adderall if you have received a methylene blue injection.
A dangerous drug interaction could occur.
You may not be able to use Adderall if you have glaucoma.

Adderall contains mixed amphetamine and dextroamphetamine salts.
Adderall contains a combination of amphetamine and dextroamphetamine.
These substances affect chemicals in the brain and nerves.
These chemicals contribute to hyperactivity and impulse control.
For ADHD, Adderall is used in children 3 to 17 years of age and in adults.
It may help increase attention and decrease impulsiveness and hyperactivity.
For narcolepsy, Adderall is used in people 6 years and older.
It is not known if Adderall is safe and effective for ADHD in children under 3 years of age.
It is not known if Adderall is safe and effective for narcolepsy in children under 6 years of age.
Adderall is a federally controlled substance (CII).

Keep Adderall in a safe place to protect it from theft.

subject: Adderall
relation_definition: The subject drug carries the warning specified by the object entity regarding use during pregnancy or while breastfeeding.
evidence_text:
Taking Adderall during pregnancy can cause premature birth, low birth weight, or withdrawal symptoms in the newborn baby.
Tell your healthcare provider if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant.
There is a pregnancy registry that collects information about the health of females exposed to Adderall and their babies.
Adderall passes into breast milk and may harm a nursing baby.
You should not breastfeed during treatment with Adderall.
Talk to your healthcare provider about the best way to feed the baby during treatment.

subject: Adderall
relation_definition: The subject drug may cause the serious or potentially dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity that requires medical attention.
evidence_text:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to Adderall.
Signs of an allergic reaction to Adderall include hives.
Signs of an allergic reaction to Adderall include difficult breathing.
Signs of an allergic reaction to Adderall include swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat.
Serious side effects:
Adderall may cause serious side effects.
Call your doctor at once if you have:
signs of heart problems, such as chest pain, trouble breathing, or feeling like you might pass out
signs of psychosis, such as hallucinations, new behavior problems, aggression, hostility, or paranoia

a seizure
muscle twitches (tics)
changes in your vision.

Slowing of growth (height and weight) in children:
Children should have their height and weight checked often during treatment.
Your healthcare provider may stop treatment if your child is not growing or gaining weight as expected.

evidence_text:
Adderall has a Boxed Warning for abuse, misuse, and addiction.
Abuse, misuse, and addiction:
Adderall has a high chance of abuse and misuse.
It may lead to substance use problems, including addiction.
Misuse and abuse of Adderall, other amphetamine-containing medicines, and methylphenidate-containing medicines can lead to overdose and death.
The risk of overdose and death is increased with higher doses.
The risk of overdose and death is increased when the medicine is used in ways that are not approved.
Examples of unapproved use include snorting or injection.
Adderall may lead to physical dependence after prolonged use, even if taken as directed.
Your healthcare provider should check you or your child for the risk of abuse, misuse, and addiction before starting treatment.
Your healthcare provider will monitor you or your child during treatment.
Tell your healthcare provider if you or your child has ever abused or been dependent on alcohol, prescription medicines, or street drugs.

subject: Adderall
relation_definition: The subject drug may cause the adverse effect or symptom specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Stimulants have caused stroke, heart attack, and sudden death in people with high blood pressure, heart disease, or a heart defect.
Your healthcare provider should check you or your child carefully for heart problems before starting Adderall.
Your healthcare provider should check blood pressure and heart rate regularly during treatment.
Call your healthcare provider right away or go to the nearest hospital emergency room if you or your child have any signs of heart problems.
These signs include chest pain, shortness of breath, or fainting during treatment.
Mental (psychiatric) problems:
Adderall may cause new or worse behavior and thought problems.
Adderall may cause new or worse bipolar illness.
Adderall may cause new psychotic symptoms, such as hearing voices, or seeing or believing things that are not real.
Adderall may cause new manic symptoms.
This is more likely if you have a history of depression, mental illness, or bipolar disorder.

subject: Adderall
relation_definition: The subject drug may cause the adverse effect or symptom specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Tell your healthcare provider about any mental problems you or your child have, or about a family history of suicide, bipolar illness, or depression.
Call your healthcare provider right away if you or your child have any new or worsening mental symptoms during treatment.
This is especially important if you experience hearing voices.
It is also important if you see or believe things that are not real.
It is also important if you have new manic symptoms.
Circulation problems:
You may have blood circulation problems that can cause numbness, pain, or discoloration in your fingers or toes.
Call your doctor right away if you have unexplained wounds appearing on your fingers or toes during treatment.
Other warnings:
Do not use Adderall if you have used an MAO inhibitor in the past 14 days.
Examples of MAO inhibitors include isocarboxazid, linezolid, phenelzine, rasagiline, selegiline, or tranylcypromine.
Do not use Adderall if you have received a methylene blue injection.
A dangerous drug interaction could occur.
You may not be able to use Adderall if you have glaucoma.

heartburn medicine

cold or allergy medicine that contains a decongestant
opioid (narcotic) medicine
seizure medicine.

You should not use ProAir RespiClick or ProAir Digihaler if you are allergic to milk proteins.
To make sure albuterol inhalation is safe for you, tell your doctor if you have:
heart disease, high blood pressure, congestive heart failure;
a heart rhythm disorder;
a seizure disorder such as epilepsy;
diabetes;
overactive thyroid; or
low levels of potassium in your blood.
Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant.
It is not known whether albuterol will harm an unborn baby.
However, having uncontrolled asthma during pregnancy may increase the risk of premature birth.
It may also increase the risk of low birth weight.
It may also increase the risk of eclampsia.
Eclampsia is dangerously high blood pressure.
Eclampsia can lead to medical problems in both mother and baby.
The benefit of preventing bronchospasm may outweigh any risks to the baby.
If you are pregnant, your name may be listed on a pregnancy registry.
The registry is used to track the effects of albuterol on the baby.

evidence_text:
Allopurinol belongs to a class of medications called xanthine oxidase inhibitors.
It works by reducing the production of uric acid in the body.
High levels of uric acid may cause gout attacks or kidney stones.
Allopurinol is used to treat gout.
Gout is a type of arthritis.
In gout, uric acid builds up in the joints.
Uric acid is a naturally occurring substance in the body.
The buildup of uric acid causes sudden attacks of redness, swelling, pain, and heat.
These attacks occur in one or more joints.
Allopurinol is used to prevent gout attacks, not to treat them once they occur.
Allopurinol does not need to be stopped during an acute flare.
Allopurinol is also used to treat high levels of uric acid.
The high levels of uric acid build up in the blood.
This buildup occurs as tumors break down.
This happens in people with certain types of cancer.
These people are being treated with chemotherapy medications.
It is also used to treat kidney stones that have come back.
This occurs in people who have high levels of uric acid in their urine.

subject: Allopurinol
object: reducing the production of uric acid in the body
relation_definition: The subject drug produces its therapeutic effect through the biological mechanism specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Allopurinol belongs to a class of medications called xanthine oxidase inhibitors.
It works by reducing the production of uric acid in the body.
High levels of uric acid may cause gout attacks or kidney stones.
Allopurinol is used to treat gout.
Gout is a type of arthritis.
In gout, uric acid builds up in the joints.
Uric acid is a naturally occurring substance in the body.
The buildup of uric acid causes sudden attacks of redness, swelling, pain, and heat.
These attacks occur in one or more joints.
Allopurinol is used to prevent gout attacks, not to treat them once they occur.
Allopurinol does not need to be stopped during an acute flare.
Allopurinol is also used to treat high levels of uric acid.
The high levels of uric acid build up in the blood.
This buildup occurs as tumors break down.
This happens in people with certain types of cancer.
These people are being treated with chemotherapy medications.
It is also used to treat kidney stones that have come back.
This occurs in people who have high levels of uric acid in their urine.

Amlodipine besylate is a prescription medicine.
It is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension).
It is used to prevent certain types of angina (chest pain).
It belongs to a class of medications called calcium channel blockers.
Amlodipine besylate works by relaxing and widening the blood vessels.
This causes blood to flow more easily.
This improves blood pressure.
Amlodipine besylate controls angina chest pain by increasing the supply of blood to the heart.
If taken regularly, this medicine controls chest pain.
It does not stop chest pain once it starts.
Your doctor may prescribe a different medication to take when you have chest pain.

Lowering blood pressure may lower your risk of a stroke or heart attack.

Amlodipine 10 mg tablets (Norvasc)
Amlodipine 2.5 mg tablets (Norvasc)
Amlodipine 1 mg/mL solution (Norliqva)

evidence_text:
Amlodipine besylate is a prescription medicine.
It is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension).
It is used to prevent certain types of angina (chest pain).
It belongs to a class of medications called calcium channel blockers.
Amlodipine besylate works by relaxing and widening the blood vessels.
This causes blood to flow more easily.
This improves blood pressure.
Amlodipine besylate controls angina chest pain by increasing the supply of blood to the heart.
If taken regularly, this medicine controls chest pain.
It does not stop chest pain once it starts.
Your doctor may prescribe a different medication to take when you have chest pain.
Amlodipine is also used alone or in combination with other medicines to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) in adults and children at least 6 years old.
Lowering blood pressure may lower your risk of a stroke or heart attack.
Amlodipine besylate is available as:
Amlodipine 5 mg tablets (Norvasc)
Amlodipine 10 mg tablets (Norvasc)
Amlodipine 2.5 mg tablets (Norvasc)
Amlodipine 1 mg/mL solution (Norliqva)

It is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension).
It is used to prevent certain types of angina (chest pain).
It belongs to a class of medications called calcium channel blockers.
Amlodipine besylate works by relaxing and widening the blood vessels.
This causes blood to flow more easily.
This improves blood pressure.
Amlodipine besylate controls angina chest pain by increasing the supply of blood to the heart.
If taken regularly, this medicine controls chest pain.
It does not stop chest pain once it starts.

Lowering blood pressure may lower your risk of a stroke or heart attack.

Amlodipine 10 mg tablets (Norvasc)
Amlodipine 2.5 mg tablets (Norvasc)
Amlodipine 1 mg/mL solution (Norliqva)

subject: clarithromycin
relation_definition: The subject drug is marketed under the brand or trade name specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Amoxicillin is a penicillin antibiotic.
Amoxicillin is used to treat bacterial infections.
The infections include tonsillitis, bronchitis, sinusitis, pneumonia, and infections of the ear, nose, throat, skin, or urinary tract.
Amoxicillin clavulanate is a combination of amoxicillin and clavulanate potassium.
The amoxicillin fights bacteria.
The clavulanate potassium helps prevent certain bacteria from becoming resistant to amoxicillin.
Amoxicillin is sometimes used together with another antibiotic called clarithromycin (Biaxin).
This combination is used to treat stomach ulcers.
The ulcers are caused by Helicobacter pylori infection.
This combination is sometimes used with a stomach acid reducer called lansoprazole (Prevacid).
Amoxicillin 500mg and 250mg are available as tablets or capsules and as an oral suspension.
Many brands and forms of amoxicillin are available.
Not all brands are listed on this leaflet.

Serious amoxicillin side effects:

These side effects affected more than 1% of patients in clinical trials.
Serious amoxicillin side effects:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to amoxicillin.
Signs of an allergic reaction to amoxicillin include hives, difficult breathing, and swelling in your face or throat.
Get emergency medical help if you have a severe skin reaction.
Signs of a severe skin reaction include fever, sore throat, burning eyes, skin pain, and a red or purple skin rash with blistering and peeling.
Call your doctor at once if you have:
severe stomach pain or vomiting (which may be signs of a serious intestinal condition); or
diarrhea that is watery or bloody (even if it occurs months after your last dose).
This is not a complete list of side effects.

You should not take apixaban if you are allergic to it or if you have active bleeding from any cause.
Apixaban can cause a serious blood clot.
This can happen if you undergo a procedure.
The procedure could be a spinal tap.
The procedure could be receiving spinal anesthesia.
Spinal anesthesia is also known as epidural.
This type of blood clot could cause permanent or long-term paralysis.
Apixaban can make it easier for you to bleed, even from a minor injury.
Call your doctor if you have any bleeding that will not stop.
Tell your doctor if you have or have ever had:
artificial heart valve;
a history of problems with your spine, a spinal surgery, or difficult or repeated spinal taps;
bleeding problems;
plan for surgery, or a medical or a dental procedure;
a thin tube (catheter) placed in your back to give you certain medicine;
antiphospholipid syndrome, an immune system disorder that increases the risk of blood clots; or
liver or kidney disease.
It is not known if apixaban will harm an unborn baby.

subject: Atorvastatin
relation_definition: The subject drug produces its therapeutic effect through the biological mechanism specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Atorvastatin works by selectively blocking HMG-CoA reductase.
HMG-CoA reductase is the key enzyme the liver uses to produce cholesterol.
By slowing this process, it reduces cholesterol production in the liver.
It increases the number of LDL receptors on liver cells.
This helps remove more LDL ("bad") cholesterol from the bloodstream.
As a result, it lowers overall LDL levels.
It decreases the number of LDL particles.
It improves the body's ability to clear cholesterol.

Bupropion is an antidepressant medication used to treat depression and seasonal affective disorder.
It also supports smoking cessation and weight management.
Bupropion is the active ingredient in Wellbutrin and Zyban.
Auvelity contains bupropion and dextromethorphan.
Contrave contains bupropion and naltrexone.
Bupropion improves mood regulation.
Bupropion improves nicotine cravings.
When combined with naltrexone, bupropion helps reduce food intake.
Bupropion is thought to work by changing levels of certain chemicals in the brain.
These chemicals include noradrenaline and dopamine.
Bupropion first became an FDA-approved medicine on 30 December 1985.

subject: nicotine replacement product
relation_definition: The subject condition or category includes the specific condition or entity specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Some people taking bupropion have severe high blood pressure.
This is especially true when using a nicotine replacement product.
The nicotine replacement product can be a patch or gum.
Your blood pressure may need to be checked before and during treatment with this medicine.
This medicine can cause you to have a false positive drug screening test (amphetamines).
If you provide a urine sample for drug screening, tell the laboratory staff you are taking this medicine.
For smoking cessation.
If you take bupropion to help you stop smoking, you may continue to smoke for about 1 week.
This may happen after you start the medicine.
Set a date to quit smoking during the second week of treatment.
Talk to your doctor if you are having trouble quitting after you have used bupropion for at least 7 to 12 weeks.
Your doctor may prescribe a nicotine replacement product (such as patches or gum) to help you stop smoking.
Start using the nicotine replacement product on the same day you stop (quit) smoking or using tobacco products.
You may have nicotine withdrawal symptoms when you stop smoking.

Tell your doctor about all medicines you use, and those you start or stop using during your treatment.

Monitor digoxin levels
MAOIs: Increased risk of hypertensive reactions can occur when used concomitantly with this medication.

Medicines that are CYP2B6 inhibitors may require dose adjustment if coadministered with CYP2B6 inhibitors.

evidence_text:
Do not use this medicine if you have used an MAO inhibitor in the past 14 days.
A dangerous drug interaction could occur.
MAO inhibitors include isocarboxazid, linezolid, methylene blue injection, phenelzine, rasagiline, selegiline, tranylcypromine, and others.
You should not take this medicine if you are allergic to it or if you have ever had:
a seizure disorder;
an eating disorder such as anorexia or bulimia; or
if you have suddenly stopped using alcohol, seizure medication, or a sedative (such as Xanax, Valium, Fiorinal, Klonopin, and others).
Do not take this medicine to treat more than one condition at a time.
If you take bupropion for depression, do not also take this medicine.
Do not take this medicine to quit smoking.
Do not take this medicine for weight management.
Tell your doctor about all of your medical conditions and the drugs you use.
To make sure this medicine is safe for you, tell your doctor if you have ever had:
a head injury, seizures, or brain or spinal cord tumor;
narrow-angle glaucoma;
heart disease, high blood pressure, or a heart attack;
diabetes;

evidence_text:
Cyclobenzaprine works by reducing the nerve signals in the brain.
These signals drive muscle tone and spasm.
This reduction allows tight, overactive muscles to relax.
It acts within the central nervous system.
It acts primarily at the level of the brain stem.
It does not act on the muscles themselves.
It does not act at the junction between nerves and muscle.
Cyclobenzaprine works through the nervous system in this way.
Therefore, it will not relieve muscle spasm caused by central nervous system disease.
Examples of such diseases include cerebral palsy or spinal cord disease.
1,2
The way cyclobenzaprine works in fibromyalgia is not known.
Laboratory studies show it blocks several receptor types.
These receptor types include serotonin (5-HT2A), histamine, and muscarinic receptors.
3
Cyclobenzaprine is chemically related to tricyclic antidepressants such as amitriptyline.
This relationship explains several of its side effects.
These side effects include drowsiness and dry mouth.
The relationship also explains some of its most important drug interactions.

evidence_text:
Cyclobenzaprine works by reducing the nerve signals in the brain.
These signals drive muscle tone and spasm.
This reduction allows tight, overactive muscles to relax.
It acts within the central nervous system.
It acts primarily at the level of the brain stem.
It does not act on the muscles themselves.
It does not act at the junction between nerves and muscle.
Cyclobenzaprine works through the nervous system in this way.
Therefore, it will not relieve muscle spasm caused by central nervous system disease.
Examples of such diseases include cerebral palsy or spinal cord disease.

The way cyclobenzaprine works in fibromyalgia is not known.
Laboratory studies show it blocks several receptor types.
These receptor types include serotonin (5-HT2A), histamine, and muscarinic receptors.

evidence_text:
Cyclobenzaprine works by reducing the nerve signals in the brain.
These signals drive muscle tone and spasm.
This reduction allows tight, overactive muscles to relax.
It acts within the central nervous system.
It acts primarily at the level of the brain stem.
It does not act on the muscles themselves.
It does not act at the junction between nerves and muscle.
Cyclobenzaprine works through the nervous system in this way.
Therefore, it will not relieve muscle spasm caused by central nervous system disease.
Examples of such diseases include cerebral palsy or spinal cord disease.
1,2
The way cyclobenzaprine works in fibromyalgia is not known.
Laboratory studies show it blocks several receptor types.
These receptor types include serotonin (5-HT2A), histamine, and muscarinic receptors.
3
Cyclobenzaprine is chemically related to tricyclic antidepressants such as amitriptyline.
This relationship explains several of its side effects.
These side effects include drowsiness and dry mouth.
The relationship also explains some of its most important drug interactions.
1,2

subject: muscle spasms
relation_definition: The subject condition or category includes the specific condition or entity specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Cyclobenzaprine is a prescription muscle relaxant.
It is used short-term to relieve muscle spasms.
The spasms are caused by sprains, strains, and injuries.
These include low back and neck pain.
It is used together with rest and physical therapy.
This combination helps relieve pain, tenderness, and limited movement.
These symptoms are caused by muscle spasm.
1,2
Cyclobenzaprine is used to treat fibromyalgia in adults.
It can help reduce pain.
For fibromyalgia, it is taken as a sublingual (under the tongue) tablet at bedtime under the brand name Tonmya.
In clinical trials, Tonmya significantly reduced fibromyalgia pain compared with placebo over 14 weeks.
Close to half of treated patients achieved at least a 30% improvement in pain.
3
The Flexeril brand has been discontinued.
Cyclobenzaprine is available as generic tablets.
Cyclobenzaprine is also available as the brand-name products Amrix and Fexmid.

Cyclobenzaprine works by reducing the nerve signals in the brain.
These signals drive muscle tone and spasm.
This reduction allows tight, overactive muscles to relax.

It does not act on the muscles themselves.
It does not act at the junction between nerves and muscle.

Therefore, it will not relieve muscle spasm caused by central nervous system disease.
Examples of such diseases include cerebral palsy or spinal cord disease.

These receptor types include serotonin (5-HT2A), histamine, and muscarinic receptors.

This relationship explains several of its side effects.
These side effects include drowsiness and dry mouth.
The relationship also explains some of its most important drug interactions.

Duloxetine is a selective serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor antidepressant (SSNRI).
Duloxetine affects chemicals in the brain that may be unbalanced in people with depression.
Duloxetine is used to treat major depressive disorder in adults.
It is also used to treat general anxiety disorder in adults and children who are at least 7 years old.
Duloxetine is also used in adults to treat nerve pain caused by diabetes (diabetic neuropathy).
It is also used to treat chronic muscle or joint pain (such as low back pain and osteoarthritis pain).
Some brands of duloxetine are also used to treat fibromyalgia (a chronic pain disorder).
Drizalma is for treating fibromyalgia only in adults.
Cymbalta may be used to treat fibromyalgia in adults and children at least 13 years old.

Fluticasone propionate is a corticosteroid that reduces inflammation in the lining of the nose.
Flonase Nasal Spray is used to treat nasal congestion, sneezing, runny nose, and itchy or watery eyes.
These symptoms are caused by seasonal or year-round allergies.
Flonase Allergy Relief is for use in adults and children who are at least 4 years old.
It is available without a prescription.

It is approved for use in adults and children 2 years of age and older.
Children's Flonase Sensimist is also for ages 2 and older.
In Flonase Sensimist labeling, relief of itchy, watery eyes applies to ages 12 and older.
The brand-name prescription version of Flonase nasal spray has been discontinued in the United States.
Generic fluticasone propionate nasal spray is still available by prescription.

evidence_text:
Flonase is a nasal spray containing fluticasone propionate.
Fluticasone propionate is a corticosteroid that reduces inflammation in the lining of the nose.
Flonase Nasal Spray is used to treat nasal congestion, sneezing, runny nose, and itchy or watery eyes.
These symptoms are caused by seasonal or year-round allergies.
Flonase Allergy Relief is for use in adults and children who are at least 4 years old.
It is available without a prescription.
Children's Flonase Allergy Relief contains the same medicine.
It is also for ages 4 and older.
Flonase Sensimist contains fluticasone furoate rather than fluticasone propionate.
It is approved for use in adults and children 2 years of age and older.
Children's Flonase Sensimist is also for ages 2 and older.
In Flonase Sensimist labeling, relief of itchy, watery eyes applies to ages 12 and older.
The brand-name prescription version of Flonase nasal spray has been discontinued in the United States.
Generic fluticasone propionate nasal spray is still available by prescription.

Before using Flonase Nasal Spray, tell your doctor if you have glaucoma or cataracts.
Tell your doctor if you have liver disease, diabetes, herpes simplex virus of your eyes, tuberculosis, or any other infection.
Tell your doctor if you have sores or ulcers inside your nose.
Tell your doctor if you have recently had injury of or surgery on your nose.
You may start to feel relief on the first day.
It can take several days of regular once-daily use before you get the full effect.
Tell your doctor if your symptoms do not improve within 7 days.
Tell your doctor if you develop new symptoms such as severe facial pain or thick nasal discharge.
Corticosteroids can affect the way your immune system responds to infection.
Avoid being near people who are sick or have infections.
Stop use and ask a doctor if you have, or come into contact with someone who has, chickenpox, measles, or tuberculosis.
Do not administer Flonase Allergy Relief Nasal Spray to a child younger than 4 years old.
Do not administer Flonase Sensimist to a child younger than 2 years.

Flonase is a nasal spray containing fluticasone propionate.
Fluticasone propionate is a corticosteroid that reduces inflammation in the lining of the nose.
Flonase Nasal Spray is used to treat nasal congestion, sneezing, runny nose, and itchy or watery eyes.
These symptoms are caused by seasonal or year-round allergies.
Flonase Allergy Relief is for use in adults and children who are at least 4 years old.
It is available without a prescription.
Children's Flonase Allergy Relief contains the same medicine.
It is also for ages 4 and older.
Flonase Sensimist contains fluticasone furoate rather than fluticasone propionate.
It is approved for use in adults and children 2 years of age and older.
Children's Flonase Sensimist is also for ages 2 and older.
In Flonase Sensimist labeling, relief of itchy, watery eyes applies to ages 12 and older.
The brand-name prescription version of Flonase nasal spray has been discontinued in the United States.
Generic fluticasone propionate nasal spray is still available by prescription.

Fluticasone propionate is a corticosteroid that reduces inflammation in the lining of the nose.
Flonase Nasal Spray is used to treat nasal congestion, sneezing, runny nose, and itchy or watery eyes.
These symptoms are caused by seasonal or year-round allergies.
Flonase Allergy Relief is for use in adults and children who are at least 4 years old.
It is available without a prescription.
Children's Flonase Allergy Relief contains the same medicine.
It is also for ages 4 and older.
Flonase Sensimist contains fluticasone furoate rather than fluticasone propionate.
It is approved for use in adults and children 2 years of age and older.
Children's Flonase Sensimist is also for ages 2 and older.
In Flonase Sensimist labeling, relief of itchy, watery eyes applies to ages 12 and older.
The brand-name prescription version of Flonase nasal spray has been discontinued in the United States.
Generic fluticasone propionate nasal spray is still available by prescription.

evidence_text:
How long does fluoxetine take to work?
:
Most people need to take fluoxetine for 4 to 6 weeks before feeling the full effects.
Some improvement in sleep, appetite, or energy levels may be noticeable within the first 1 to 2 weeks.
Mood and motivation typically take longer to improve.
For obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), it may take 5 weeks or longer to see the full benefit.
It is important to keep taking this medicine as prescribed.
You should continue even if you do not feel immediate improvement.
Do not stop without speaking to your doctor first.
Is fluoxetine a controlled substance?
:
No, fluoxetine is not a controlled substance.
It is not classified under the DEA Controlled Substances Act.
This means it does not have recognized potential for dependence or abuse.
Drugs like opioids or benzodiazepines have this potential.
It is, however, a prescription-only medicine.
It still requires a valid prescription from a licensed healthcare provider.
Is fluoxetine an SSRI?
:
Yes, fluoxetine is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI).

Contact your doctor right away if you experience any of the following.
Boxed warning:
Fluoxetine carries a boxed warning, the FDA's most serious warning, regarding suicidal thoughts and behavior.
Antidepressants may increase the risk of suicidal thoughts in children, adolescents, and young adults.
Fluoxetine is an antidepressant.
The risk is particularly high in the first few months of treatment.
The risk is also high when the dose is changed.
This risk was not seen in adults over 24.
Adults 65 and older actually showed a reduced risk.
Anyone starting this medicine should be closely monitored for worsening mood or new or worsening suicidal thoughts.
Families and caregivers should stay in regular contact with the prescriber.

Serotonin syndrome: A potentially life-threatening condition that can occur when serotonin builds up to dangerous levels.
This can occur when taken alone.
It is more likely when taken with other serotonergic medications.

How long does fluoxetine take to work?
:
Most people need to take fluoxetine for 4 to 6 weeks before feeling the full effects.
Some improvement in sleep, appetite, or energy levels may be noticeable within the first 1 to 2 weeks.
Mood and motivation typically take longer to improve.
For obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), it may take 5 weeks or longer to see the full benefit.
It is important to keep taking this medicine as prescribed.
You should continue even if you do not feel immediate improvement.
Do not stop without speaking to your doctor first.
Is fluoxetine a controlled substance?
:
No, fluoxetine is not a controlled substance.
It is not classified under the DEA Controlled Substances Act.
This means it does not have recognized potential for dependence or abuse.
Drugs like opioids or benzodiazepines have this potential.
It is, however, a prescription-only medicine.
It still requires a valid prescription from a licensed healthcare provider.
Is fluoxetine an SSRI?
:
Yes, fluoxetine is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI).

:

However, some people do experience weight changes over longer-term use.
If you notice significant weight changes while taking this medicine, speak to your doctor.
Dose adjustments or alternative treatments may be available.

40mg of fluoxetine is considered a moderate maintenance dose in adults for major depressive disorder (MDD) and OCD.
The standard starting dose for most conditions is 20mg per day.
The starting dose for panic disorder is 10mg.
If symptoms have not improved after several weeks, the dose may be increased.

Does fluoxetine cause weight gain?
:
Fluoxetine is less likely to cause weight gain than many other antidepressants.
In the short term, it can actually cause mild weight loss.

Most people need to take fluoxetine for 4 to 6 weeks before feeling the full effects.
Some improvement in sleep, appetite, or energy levels may be noticeable within the first 1 to 2 weeks.
Mood and motivation typically take longer to improve.
For obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), it may take 5 weeks or longer to see the full benefit.
It is important to keep taking this medicine as prescribed.
You should continue even if you do not feel immediate improvement.
Do not stop without speaking to your doctor first.
Is fluoxetine a controlled substance?
:
No, fluoxetine is not a controlled substance.
It is not classified under the DEA Controlled Substances Act.
This means it does not have recognized potential for dependence or abuse.
Drugs like opioids or benzodiazepines have this potential.
It is, however, a prescription-only medicine.
It still requires a valid prescription from a licensed healthcare provider.
Is fluoxetine an SSRI?
:
Yes, fluoxetine is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI).

How long does fluoxetine take to work?
:
Most people need to take fluoxetine for 4 to 6 weeks before feeling the full effects.
Some improvement in sleep, appetite, or energy levels may be noticeable within the first 1 to 2 weeks.
Mood and motivation typically take longer to improve.
For obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), it may take 5 weeks or longer to see the full benefit.
It is important to keep taking this medicine as prescribed.
You should continue even if you do not feel immediate improvement.
Do not stop without speaking to your doctor first.
Is fluoxetine a controlled substance?
:
No, fluoxetine is not a controlled substance.
It is not classified under the DEA Controlled Substances Act.
This means it does not have recognized potential for dependence or abuse.
Drugs like opioids or benzodiazepines have this potential.
It is, however, a prescription-only medicine.
It still requires a valid prescription from a licensed healthcare provider.
Is fluoxetine an SSRI?
:
Yes, fluoxetine is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI).

Like all medications, Prozac carries some important warnings you should be aware of before and during treatment.
Contact your doctor right away if you experience any of the following.
Boxed warning:
Fluoxetine carries a boxed warning, the FDA's most serious warning, regarding suicidal thoughts and behavior.
Antidepressants may increase the risk of suicidal thoughts in children, adolescents, and young adults.
Fluoxetine is an antidepressant.
The risk is particularly high in the first few months of treatment.
The risk is also high when the dose is changed.
This risk was not seen in adults over 24.
Adults 65 and older actually showed a reduced risk.
Anyone starting this medicine should be closely monitored for worsening mood or new or worsening suicidal thoughts.
Families and caregivers should stay in regular contact with the prescriber.
Other warnings:
Serotonin syndrome: A potentially life-threatening condition that can occur when serotonin builds up to dangerous levels.
This can occur when taken alone.
It is more likely when taken with other serotonergic medications.

Major depressive disorder (MDD) for acute and maintenance treatment in adults and children aged 8 years and older
Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) for acute and maintenance treatment in adults and children aged 7 years and older
Bulimia nervosa for acute and maintenance treatment of binge-eating and purging in adults with moderate to severe bulimia
Panic disorder for the treatment of panic attacks in adults

Acute treatment of depressive episodes associated with Bipolar I disorder (depressive episodes) in adults and children aged 10 years and older

How long does fluoxetine take to work?
:
Most people need to take fluoxetine for 4 to 6 weeks before feeling the full effects.
Some improvement in sleep, appetite, or energy levels may be noticeable within the first 1 to 2 weeks.
Mood and motivation typically take longer to improve.
For obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), it may take 5 weeks or longer to see the full benefit.
It is important to keep taking this medicine as prescribed.
You should continue even if you do not feel immediate improvement.
Do not stop without speaking to your doctor first.
Is fluoxetine a controlled substance?
:
No, fluoxetine is not a controlled substance.
It is not classified under the DEA Controlled Substances Act.
This means it does not have recognized potential for dependence or abuse.
Drugs like opioids or benzodiazepines have this potential.
It is, however, a prescription-only medicine.
It still requires a valid prescription from a licensed healthcare provider.
Is fluoxetine an SSRI?
:
Yes, fluoxetine is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI).

How long does fluoxetine stay in your system?
:
Fluoxetine stays in your system longer than most other antidepressants.
After stopping this medicine, it takes approximately 1 to 4 days for the drug itself to be reduced by half.
Fluoxetine converts in the body to an active metabolite called norfluoxetine.
Norfluoxetine has a much longer half-life of 4 to 16 days.
This means this medicine and its active metabolite can remain detectable in your system.
They can remain detectable for up to 5 weeks.
This duration is after your last dose.
This is clinically important for two reasons:
Switching medications requires a washout period.
This applies if you are switching from fluoxetine to certain other antidepressants.
These other antidepressants include MAOIs.
Your doctor will require a washout period of at least 5 weeks.
This period allows fluoxetine to fully clear your system.
This avoids dangerous drug interactions.

diarrhea, constipation, loss of appetite
numbness or tingling
headache, dizziness
blurred vision
redness, bruising, swelling, or pain where a subcutaneous dose is given.
Serious furosemide side effects:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to furosemide, such as hives, difficult breathing, or swelling in your face or throat.
Get emergency medical help if you have a severe skin reaction, such as fever, sore throat, burning eyes, skin pain, or a red or purple skin rash with blistering and peeling.

a light-headed feeling, like you might pass out

pale skin, easy bruising, unusual bleeding
high blood sugar, with increased thirst, increased urination, dry mouth, or fruity breath odor

relation_definition: The subject drug leads to or results in the effect or condition specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Gabapentin works by calming overactive electrical signals in the brain and nervous system.
It does this by binding to the alpha-2-delta subunit of calcium channels in nerve cells.
The alpha-2-delta subunit is thought to normalize chemical signals nerves send to each other.
This results in a calmer, less excitable nerve circuit.
That same effect helps in different ways depending on what gabapentin is treating:
Epilepsy - dampens the runaway electrical firing that causes seizures.
Postherpetic neuralgia (shingles nerve pain) - reduces the abnormal pain signals from nerves damaged by shingles.
Restless legs syndrome (gabapentin enacarbil / Horizant) has an exact mechanism that is less clear.
The same calming effect on overactive nerves is thought to ease the urge-to-move sensation.
Gabapentin is not an opioid, sedative, or anti-inflammatory painkiller.
It works directly on the nerves.
It helps nerve-related pain.

evidence_text:
Gabapentin works by calming overactive electrical signals in the brain and nervous system.
It does this by binding to the alpha-2-delta subunit of calcium channels in nerve cells.
The alpha-2-delta subunit is thought to normalize chemical signals nerves send to each other.
This results in a calmer, less excitable nerve circuit.
That same effect helps in different ways depending on what gabapentin is treating:
Epilepsy - dampens the runaway electrical firing that causes seizures.
Postherpetic neuralgia (shingles nerve pain) - reduces the abnormal pain signals from nerves damaged by shingles.
Restless legs syndrome (gabapentin enacarbil / Horizant) has an exact mechanism that is less clear.
The same calming effect on overactive nerves is thought to ease the urge-to-move sensation.
Gabapentin is not an opioid, sedative, or anti-inflammatory painkiller.
It works directly on the nerves.
It helps nerve-related pain.
It isn't useful for everyday pain.

subject: gabapentin enacarbil
relation_definition: The subject drug has the benefit or therapeutic effect specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Gabapentin works by calming overactive electrical signals in the brain and nervous system.
It does this by binding to the alpha-2-delta subunit of calcium channels in nerve cells.
The alpha-2-delta subunit is thought to normalize chemical signals nerves send to each other.
This results in a calmer, less excitable nerve circuit.
That same effect helps in different ways depending on what gabapentin is treating:
Epilepsy - dampens the runaway electrical firing that causes seizures.
Postherpetic neuralgia (shingles nerve pain) - reduces the abnormal pain signals from nerves damaged by shingles.
Restless legs syndrome (gabapentin enacarbil / Horizant) has an exact mechanism that is less clear.
The same calming effect on overactive nerves is thought to ease the urge-to-move sensation.
Gabapentin is not an opioid, sedative, or anti-inflammatory painkiller.
It works directly on the nerves.
It helps nerve-related pain.
It isn't useful for everyday pain.
Everyday pain includes headaches.
Everyday pain includes sprains.

subject: Gabapentin
relation_definition: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Gabapentin is available as capsules, tablets, extended-release tablets, and an oral solution.
Strengths vary by product.
Different products are not interchangeable.
Neurontin and generic gabapentin
oral capsules 100 mg, 300 mg, 400 mg
oral tablets 600 mg, 800 mg
oral solution 250 mg/5 mL
Relgaabi
oral capsules 100 mg, 200 mg, 300 mg, 400 mg
Gralise
extended-release tablets 300 mg, 450 mg, 600 mg, 750 mg, and 900 mg
Horizant (gabapentin enacarbil)
extended-release tablets 300 mg, 600 mg
Note: The Horizant strengths refer to gabapentin enacarbil.
The Horizant strengths do not refer to gabapentin itself.
Therefore, Horizant doses do not correspond milligram-for-milligram to other gabapentin products.

subject: everyday pain
relation_definition: The subject condition or category includes the specific condition or entity specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Gabapentin works by calming overactive electrical signals in the brain and nervous system.
It does this by binding to the alpha-2-delta subunit of calcium channels in nerve cells.
The alpha-2-delta subunit is thought to normalize chemical signals nerves send to each other.
This results in a calmer, less excitable nerve circuit.
That same effect helps in different ways depending on what gabapentin is treating:
Epilepsy - dampens the runaway electrical firing that causes seizures.
Postherpetic neuralgia (shingles nerve pain) - reduces the abnormal pain signals from nerves damaged by shingles.
Restless legs syndrome (gabapentin enacarbil / Horizant) has an exact mechanism that is less clear.
The same calming effect on overactive nerves is thought to ease the urge-to-move sensation.
Gabapentin is not an opioid, sedative, or anti-inflammatory painkiller.
It works directly on the nerves.
It helps nerve-related pain.

Gabapentin works by calming overactive electrical signals in the brain and nervous system.

The same calming effect on overactive nerves is thought to ease the urge-to-move sensation.

evidence_text:
Gabapentin works by calming overactive electrical signals in the brain and nervous system.
It does this by binding to the alpha-2-delta subunit of calcium channels in nerve cells.
The alpha-2-delta subunit is thought to normalize chemical signals nerves send to each other.
This results in a calmer, less excitable nerve circuit.
That same effect helps in different ways depending on what gabapentin is treating:
Epilepsy - dampens the runaway electrical firing that causes seizures.
Postherpetic neuralgia (shingles nerve pain) - reduces the abnormal pain signals from nerves damaged by shingles.
Restless legs syndrome (gabapentin enacarbil / Horizant) has an exact mechanism that is less clear.
The same calming effect on overactive nerves is thought to ease the urge-to-move sensation.
Gabapentin is not an opioid, sedative, or anti-inflammatory painkiller.
It works directly on the nerves.
It helps nerve-related pain.
It isn't useful for everyday pain.
Everyday pain includes headaches.
Everyday pain includes sprains.

evidence_text:
Taking gabapentin with other medicines can cause dangerous side effects.
These other medicines make you drowsy or slow your breathing.
The side effects include life-threatening breathing problems.
Ask your doctor before using gabapentin with:
opioid pain medicines such as hydrocodone, oxycodone, morphine, or buprenorphine
sleeping pills such as zolpidem
anxiety medicines such as lorazepam and other benzodiazepines
muscle relaxers, sedatives, or other seizure medicines that cause drowsiness
Avoid drinking alcohol while taking gabapentin, because it can add to these effects.
Some medicines change the amount of gabapentin in your body:
Antacids that contain aluminum or magnesium (such as Maalox) can reduce gabapentin absorption.
Take gabapentin at least 2 hours after an antacid.
Morphine can increase gabapentin levels.
This may increase drowsiness.
This may also increase the risk of breathing problems.
Your doctor may adjust your dose.
Gabapentin does not usually interact with other seizure medicines.

subject: Hydrochlorothiazide
relation_definition: The subject drug is given through the route of administration specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Hydrochlorothiazide is a thiazide diuretic.
It is often called a water pill.
It is used to treat high blood pressure.
It is used to reduce a build-up of fluid in the body.
This build-up of fluid is called edema.
It works by making the kidneys pass more salt and water out of the body.
You urinate more.
Hydrochlorothiazide is often shortened to HCTZ on prescriptions and medical records.
It is available as a tablet, capsule, and liquid (suspension) taken by mouth.
It is usually taken once or twice a day.
Hydrochlorothiazide is available as:
oral tablet (12.5 mg, 25 mg, and 50 mg)
oral capsule (12.5 mg)
powder for oral suspension (10 mg/mL)
Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ) brand names included HydroDIURIL tablets (discontinued).
Esidrix (discontinued) was a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Microzide capsules (discontinued) were a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Now generic tablets and capsules are available.
The brand name of hydrochlorothiazide oral suspension is Inzirqo.
Hydrochlorothiazide is also an ingredient in many combination blood pressure medicines.

subject: Hydrochlorothiazide
relation_definition: The subject drug influences or alters the function or levels of the chemical or entity specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
It can make existing gout worse.
The medicine also affects calcium.
The medicine is stopped before parathyroid function tests.
Tell any doctor arranging tests that you take it.
Your doctor will check these levels from time to time.
Skin cancer risk:
Long-term use of hydrochlorothiazide is linked to a small increase in the risk of non-melanoma skin cancer.
The risk is mainly due to squamous cell carcinoma.
In a large safety study, the increase was about 1 extra case per 16,000 people per year.
This figure rose to about 1 extra case per 6,700 people per year among white patients who had taken a total of 50,000 mg or more.
Protect your skin from the sun.
Wear protective clothing and use sunscreen.
Avoid sunlamps and tanning beds.
Have regular skin checks.
Tell your doctor about any new or changing skin growth, or a sore that does not heal.
Lupus and allergic reactions:
Thiazide diuretics have been reported to worsen lupus or bring it on.
Sensitivity reactions can happen whether or not you have a history of allergies or asthma.

Fluid and salt imbalance:
Hydrochlorothiazide can lower the levels of potassium, sodium, magnesium and chloride in your blood.
Low potassium (hypokalemia) is the most common of these.
It is more likely at higher doses.

subject: Hydrochlorothiazide

evidence_text:
Hydrochlorothiazide is a thiazide diuretic.
It is often called a water pill.
It is used to treat high blood pressure.
It is used to reduce a build-up of fluid in the body.
This build-up of fluid is called edema.
It works by making the kidneys pass more salt and water out of the body.
You urinate more.
Hydrochlorothiazide is often shortened to HCTZ on prescriptions and medical records.
It is available as a tablet, capsule, and liquid (suspension) taken by mouth.
It is usually taken once or twice a day.
Hydrochlorothiazide is available as:
oral tablet (12.5 mg, 25 mg, and 50 mg)
oral capsule (12.5 mg)
powder for oral suspension (10 mg/mL)
Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ) brand names included HydroDIURIL tablets (discontinued).
Esidrix (discontinued) was a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Microzide capsules (discontinued) were a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Now generic tablets and capsules are available.
The brand name of hydrochlorothiazide oral suspension is Inzirqo.
Hydrochlorothiazide is also an ingredient in many combination blood pressure medicines.

Your doctor will choose the smallest dose that controls your condition.

Follow your prescription label and do not change your dose yourself.
HCTZ dose for high blood pressure (adults):
Tablets: The starting dose is hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg once a day.
The dose may be increased to 50 mg a day.
The dose is taken as a single dose or split into two doses.
Doses above 50 mg a day are often associated with a marked drop in blood potassium.
Most people do not need more than 50 mg a day when hydrochlorothiazide is taken alongside other blood pressure medicines
The starting dose is a hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg capsule once a day.
It can be taken on its own or with other blood pressure medicines.
Total daily doses above 50 mg are not recommended.
Capsules are approved for high blood pressure only, not for fluid retention.
HCTZ dose for fluid retention (adults):
Tablets: The usual dose is hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg to 100 mg a day, taken as a single dose or split into two doses.
Many people with fluid retention respond to intermittent treatment.

:
Hydrochlorothiazide is not a weight loss medicine.
Some people see the number on the scales drop in the first days or weeks of treatment.
This is extra fluid leaving the body.
This is not any loss of body fat.
The weight loss levels off.
Do not take hydrochlorothiazide to lose weight.
Can you drink alcohol while taking hydrochlorothiazide?
:
Alcohol can make the drop in blood pressure that happens when you stand up worse.
This drop in blood pressure may leave you feeling dizzy or faint.
The same applies to barbiturates and opioid pain medicines.
Tell your doctor how much you drink so they can advise you.
Does hydrochlorothiazide lower your potassium?
:
Yes.
Hydrochlorothiazide can lower blood potassium.
This condition is known as hypokalemia.
This effect is more likely at higher doses.
This effect is more likely when fluid is lost quickly.
This effect is more likely if you have severe cirrhosis.
This effect is more likely after taking the medicine for a long time.
Your doctor will check your potassium with blood tests.

If you have liver disease, small changes in fluid and salt balance can trigger a serious complication.
The complication is called hepatic coma.
Your doctor will monitor your kidney function and watch for changes in alertness.
Sudden vision changes need urgent care:
Rarely, hydrochlorothiazide causes sudden short-sightedness (acute myopia).
It also causes a sharp rise in pressure inside the eye (acute angle-closure glaucoma).
These side effects usually occur within hours to weeks of starting the medicine.
Stop taking it.
Get medical help immediately if your vision drops suddenly or your eye hurts.
Left untreated, this can cause permanent loss of vision.
A history of allergy to sulfa medicines or penicillin may increase the risk.
Blood sugar, cholesterol, uric acid and calcium:
Hydrochlorothiazide can raise blood sugar, cholesterol, triglycerides, uric acid and calcium.
Your diabetes medicine or insulin dose may need adjusting.
Diabetes that was previously unnoticed can become apparent during treatment.
The rise in uric acid is related to the dose.
It can cause gout.

drowsiness, restlessness or confusion

nausea or vomiting
seizures

Does hydrochlorothiazide cause weight loss?
:
Hydrochlorothiazide is not a weight loss medicine.
Some people see the number on the scales drop in the first days or weeks of treatment.
This is extra fluid leaving the body.
This is not any loss of body fat.
The weight loss levels off.
Do not take hydrochlorothiazide to lose weight.
Can you drink alcohol while taking hydrochlorothiazide?
:
Alcohol can make the drop in blood pressure that happens when you stand up worse.
This drop in blood pressure may leave you feeling dizzy or faint.
The same applies to barbiturates and opioid pain medicines.
Tell your doctor how much you drink so they can advise you.

:
Yes.
Hydrochlorothiazide can lower blood potassium.
This condition is known as hypokalemia.
This effect is more likely at higher doses.
This effect is more likely when fluid is lost quickly.
This effect is more likely if you have severe cirrhosis.
This effect is more likely after taking the medicine for a long time.
Your doctor will check your potassium with blood tests.

subject: Hydrochlorothiazide
relation_definition: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Hydrochlorothiazide is a thiazide diuretic.
It is often called a water pill.
It is used to treat high blood pressure.
It is used to reduce a build-up of fluid in the body.
This build-up of fluid is called edema.
It works by making the kidneys pass more salt and water out of the body.
You urinate more.
Hydrochlorothiazide is often shortened to HCTZ on prescriptions and medical records.
It is available as a tablet, capsule, and liquid (suspension) taken by mouth.
It is usually taken once or twice a day.
Hydrochlorothiazide is available as:
oral tablet (12.5 mg, 25 mg, and 50 mg)
oral capsule (12.5 mg)
powder for oral suspension (10 mg/mL)
Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ) brand names included HydroDIURIL tablets (discontinued).
Esidrix (discontinued) was a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Microzide capsules (discontinued) were a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Now generic tablets and capsules are available.
The brand name of hydrochlorothiazide oral suspension is Inzirqo.
Hydrochlorothiazide is also an ingredient in many combination blood pressure medicines.

evidence_text:
Hydrochlorothiazide is approved to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) and fluid retention (edema) in certain patients.
High blood pressure:
HCTZ is used to manage high blood pressure (hypertension), either on its own or alongside other blood pressure medicines.
Lowering blood pressure reduces the risk of fatal and non-fatal cardiovascular events, mainly strokes and heart attacks.
All three forms of hydrochlorothiazide, tablets, capsules and the oral suspension, are approved for high blood pressure in adults.
The oral suspension is also approved for children.
Fluid retention:
Hydrochlorothiazide tablets are used to treat a build-up of fluid (edema) associated with:
congestive heart failure
cirrhosis of the liver
kidney conditions, including nephrotic syndrome, acute glomerulonephritis and chronic kidney failure
treatment with corticosteroid or estrogen medicines
The HCTZ oral suspension is approved for fluid retention.
The fluid retention is associated with congestive heart failure, cirrhosis of the liver, and kidney disease.
Kidney disease includes nephrotic syndrome.

Does hydrochlorothiazide cause weight loss?
:
Hydrochlorothiazide is not a weight loss medicine.
Some people see the number on the scales drop in the first days or weeks of treatment.
This is extra fluid leaving the body.
This is not any loss of body fat.
The weight loss levels off.
Do not take hydrochlorothiazide to lose weight.
Can you drink alcohol while taking hydrochlorothiazide?
:
Alcohol can make the drop in blood pressure that happens when you stand up worse.
This drop in blood pressure may leave you feeling dizzy or faint.
The same applies to barbiturates and opioid pain medicines.
Tell your doctor how much you drink so they can advise you.
Does hydrochlorothiazide lower your potassium?
:
Yes.
Hydrochlorothiazide can lower blood potassium.
This condition is known as hypokalemia.
This effect is more likely at higher doses.
This effect is more likely when fluid is lost quickly.
This effect is more likely if you have severe cirrhosis.
This effect is more likely after taking the medicine for a long time.
Your doctor will check your potassium with blood tests.

subject: Hydrochlorothiazide
relation_definition: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the disease or medical condition specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Hydrochlorothiazide is a thiazide diuretic.
It is often called a water pill.
It is used to treat high blood pressure.
It is used to reduce a build-up of fluid in the body.
This build-up of fluid is called edema.
It works by making the kidneys pass more salt and water out of the body.
You urinate more.
Hydrochlorothiazide is often shortened to HCTZ on prescriptions and medical records.
It is available as a tablet, capsule, and liquid (suspension) taken by mouth.
It is usually taken once or twice a day.
Hydrochlorothiazide is available as:
oral tablet (12.5 mg, 25 mg, and 50 mg)
oral capsule (12.5 mg)
powder for oral suspension (10 mg/mL)
Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ) brand names included HydroDIURIL tablets (discontinued).
Esidrix (discontinued) was a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Microzide capsules (discontinued) were a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Now generic tablets and capsules are available.
The brand name of hydrochlorothiazide oral suspension is Inzirqo.
Hydrochlorothiazide is also an ingredient in many combination blood pressure medicines.

subject: Hydrochlorothiazide
relation_definition: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition or characteristic specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Do not take hydrochlorothiazide if you are unable to pass urine (anuria).
Do not take hydrochlorothiazide if you are allergic to hydrochlorothiazide or to other sulfonamide-derived medicines (sometimes called sulfa drugs).
Before you start HCTZ, tell your doctor if you have or have ever had:
kidney disease or reduced kidney function
liver disease, including cirrhosis
diabetes
gout or high uric acid levels
high cholesterol or high triglycerides
high calcium levels or a parathyroid gland disorder
low potassium or low sodium levels
lupus (systemic lupus erythematosus)
glaucoma
an allergy to sulfa medicines or to penicillin
Also tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding.
Hydrochlorothiazide may cause jaundice or bleeding problems in a newborn.
The medicine can pass into breast milk.
The medicine may cause serious side effects in a nursing baby.
You and your doctor should decide whether you will take this medicine.
You and your doctor should decide whether you will breastfeed.

subject: Hydrochlorothiazide

evidence_text:
Hydrochlorothiazide is approved to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) and fluid retention (edema) in certain patients.
High blood pressure:
HCTZ is used to manage high blood pressure (hypertension), either on its own or alongside other blood pressure medicines.
Lowering blood pressure reduces the risk of fatal and non-fatal cardiovascular events, mainly strokes and heart attacks.
All three forms of hydrochlorothiazide, tablets, capsules and the oral suspension, are approved for high blood pressure in adults.
The oral suspension is also approved for children.
Fluid retention:
Hydrochlorothiazide tablets are used to treat a build-up of fluid (edema) associated with:
congestive heart failure
cirrhosis of the liver
kidney conditions, including nephrotic syndrome, acute glomerulonephritis and chronic kidney failure
treatment with corticosteroid or estrogen medicines
The HCTZ oral suspension is approved for fluid retention.
The fluid retention is associated with congestive heart failure, cirrhosis of the liver, and kidney disease.
Kidney disease includes nephrotic syndrome.

Are allergic to any of its ingredients.
Before taking hydrocodone and acetaminophen, tell your healthcare provider if you have a history of:
Head injury, seizures
Liver, kidney, thyroid problems
Problems urinating
Pancreas or gallbladder problems
Abuse of street or prescription drugs, alcohol addiction, or mental health problems.
Tell your healthcare provider if you are:
Pregnant or planning to become pregnant.
Prolonged use of hydrocodone and acetaminophen during pregnancy can cause withdrawal symptoms in your newborn baby.
These symptoms could be life-threatening if not recognized and treated.
Breastfeeding.
Hydrocodone and acetaminophen pass into breast milk and may harm your baby.
Carefully observe infants for increased sleepiness (more than usual), breathing difficulties, or limpness.
Seek immediate medical care if you notice these signs.

The possible side effects of hydrocodone and acetaminophen are constipation, nausea, sleepiness, vomiting, tiredness, headache, dizziness, and abdominal pain.
Call your healthcare provider if you have any of these symptoms and they are severe.
Get emergency medical help if you have:
Trouble breathing
Shortness of breath
Fast heartbeat
Chest pain
Swelling of your face, tongue, or throat
Extreme drowsiness
Light-headedness when changing positions
Feeling faint
Agitation
High body temperature
Trouble walking
Stiff muscles
Mental changes such as confusion.
These are not all the possible side effects of hydrocodone and acetaminophen.
Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
You may report side effects to the FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

Hydroxyzine is thought to work by quieting activity in certain deeper regions of the brain.
These regions are located below the outer layer known as the cortex.

It does not work by slowing down the outer layer of the brain.

Hydroxyzine widens the airways (bronchodilation).
Hydroxyzine reduces pain.

Hydroxyzine is not chemically related to benzodiazepines, phenothiazines, reserpine, or meprobamate.

relation_definition: The subject drug produces its therapeutic effect through the biological mechanism specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Ibuprofen is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID).
It works by reducing hormones that cause inflammation and pain in the body.
Ibuprofen is used to reduce fever.
Ibuprofen is used to treat pain or inflammation.
The pain or inflammation is caused by many conditions.
These conditions include headache, toothache, back pain, arthritis, menstrual cramps, or minor injury.
Ibuprofen is used in adults and children.
Some formulations are also used in premature babies to close a certain heart defect.

subject: ibuprofen
object: can cause serious heart or kidney problems in the unborn baby
relation_definition: The subject drug carries the warning specified by the object entity regarding use during pregnancy or while breastfeeding.
evidence_text:
You should not use ibuprofen if you are allergic to it.
You should not use ibuprofen if you have ever had an asthma attack or severe allergic reaction after taking aspirin or an NSAID.
Ask a doctor or pharmacist if this medicine is safe to use if you have ever had:
heart disease, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, diabetes, or if you smoke;
a heart attack, stroke, or blood clot;
stomach ulcers or bleeding;
liver or kidney disease;
asthma; or
if you take aspirin to prevent heart attack or stroke.
Ask a doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant or breastfeeding.
If you are pregnant, you should not take ibuprofen unless your doctor tells you to.
Taking an NSAID at 20 weeks or later in pregnancy can cause serious heart or kidney problems in the unborn baby and possible complications with your pregnancy.
Do not take ibuprofen after 30 weeks of pregnancy.
Ibuprofen may cause a temporary delay in ovulation.
This delay can make it harder to get pregnant.
Tell your doctor if you are having trouble getting pregnant.

subject: ibuprofen

evidence_text:
Ibuprofen is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID).
It works by reducing hormones that cause inflammation and pain in the body.
Ibuprofen is used to reduce fever.
Ibuprofen is used to treat pain or inflammation.
The pain or inflammation is caused by many conditions.
These conditions include headache, toothache, back pain, arthritis, menstrual cramps, or minor injury.

subject: ibuprofen
relation_definition: The subject drug carries a safety warning or precaution about the risk or situation specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Ibuprofen can increase your risk of fatal heart attack, heart failure, or stroke.
Do not use this medicine just before or after heart bypass surgery (coronary artery bypass graft, or CABG).
Avoid taking ibuprofen after a recent heart attack, unless your doctor tells you to.
Ibuprofen may also cause stomach or intestinal bleeding.
This bleeding can be fatal.
These conditions can occur without warning while you are using this medicine, especially in older adults.
Do not take more than your recommended dose.
An ibuprofen overdose can damage your stomach or intestines.
Use only the smallest amount of medication needed to get relief from your pain, swelling, or fever.

Follow all directions on your prescription label and read all medication guides or instruction sheets.
Use the medicine exactly as directed.
Ask your doctor or pharmacist if you don't understand how to use an injection.
Prepare an injection only when you are ready to give it.
Do not use it if the medicine looks cloudy, has changed colors, or has particles in it.
Insulin glargine is injected under the skin, using a syringe or insulin pen, once per day at the same time of day.
Insulin can be injected into your upper legs (thighs), upper arms, or stomach area (abdomen).
Do not inject into the same place two times in a row.
Avoid injecting into skin that is damaged, tender, bruised, pitted, thickened, scaly, or has a scar or hard lump.
When treating type 1 diabetes, use your short-acting insulin before meals as directed by your doctor.
Insulin glargine must not be given with an insulin pump or mixed with other insulins.

Your dose needs may change if you switch to a different brand, strength, or form of this medicine.

Insulin glargine is a long-acting insulin.
It is used to treat type 1 and type 2 diabetes in certain patients.
The treatment aims to improve and maintain blood glucose levels.
Insulin glargine is a man-made form of human insulin.
It is used once daily.
It provides a base level of insulin.
This insulin keeps working for 24 hours or longer.
Insulin glargine is available under the brand names Lantus, Basaglar, Toujeo, Semglee, and Rezvoglar.
Langlara is an interchangeable biosimilar to Lantus that was FDA-approved on May 4, 2026.
Rezvoglar, Lantus, Langlara, Semglee, and Toujeo are FDA-approved.
They are approved for use in adult and pediatric patients.
These patients have type 1 and type 2 diabetes.
Basasglar is FDA-approved to be used by adults for type 2 diabetes.
It is also approved for adults and pediatric patients with type 1 diabetes.
In patients with type 1 diabetes, insulin glargine must be used together with a short-acting insulin.

Avoid medication errors by using only the medicine your doctor prescribes.
If you use an injection pen, use only the injection pen that comes with insulin glargine.
Attach a new needle before each use.
Do not transfer the insulin from the pen into a syringe.
Never share an injection pen, even if you changed the needle.
Sharing these devices can pass infections from person to person.
Blood sugar can be affected by stress, illness, surgery, exercise, alcohol use, or skipping meals.
Low blood sugar (hypoglycemia) can make you feel very hungry, dizzy, irritable, or shaky.
To quickly treat hypoglycemia, eat or drink hard candy, crackers, raisins, fruit juice, or non-diet soda.
Your doctor may prescribe glucagon injections in case of severe hypoglycemia.
Tell your doctor if you have frequent symptoms of high blood sugar (hyperglycemia), such as increased thirst or urination.
Ask your doctor before changing your medication dosage.
Wear a medical alert tag or carry an ID card to let others know you have diabetes.

subject: Insulin glargine
object: improve and maintain blood glucose levels
relation_definition: The subject drug may be used for the medical purpose or indication specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Insulin glargine is a long-acting insulin.
It is used to treat type 1 and type 2 diabetes in certain patients.
The treatment aims to improve and maintain blood glucose levels.
Insulin glargine is a man-made form of human insulin.
It is used once daily.
It provides a base level of insulin.
This insulin keeps working for 24 hours or longer.
Insulin glargine is available under the brand names Lantus, Basaglar, Toujeo, Semglee, and Rezvoglar.
Langlara is an interchangeable biosimilar to Lantus that was FDA-approved on May 4, 2026.
Rezvoglar, Lantus, Langlara, Semglee, and Toujeo are FDA-approved.
They are approved for use in adult and pediatric patients.
These patients have type 1 and type 2 diabetes.
Basasglar is FDA-approved to be used by adults for type 2 diabetes.
It is also approved for adults and pediatric patients with type 1 diabetes.
In patients with type 1 diabetes, insulin glargine must be used together with a short-acting insulin.

evidence_text:
Avoid the following food products within 1 hour of taking oral levothyroxine.
If you do not avoid these products, the medication will not be as effective.
The food products to avoid are grapefruit juice, infant soy formula, soybean flour, cottonseed meal, walnuts, and high-fiber foods.
Grapefruit juice can both delay absorption and reduce the amount of levothyroxine that gets into your body.
If you eat or drink any of these regularly, tell your doctor.
Your dose may need adjusting.

subject: Patient
relation_definition: Patients taking the subject drug should tell their doctor about the condition or circumstance specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
It may increase the risk of pre-eclampsia.
It may increase the risk of stillbirth.
It may increase the risk of premature birth.
Untreated hypothyroidism can affect the baby's brain development.
The benefit of treating hypothyroidism outweighs these risks.
Levothyroxine should not be stopped during pregnancy.
Your dose needs are often higher during pregnancy.
Your doctor will check your thyroid blood tests as soon as your pregnancy is confirmed.
Your doctor will check your thyroid blood tests at least once in each trimester.
Your doctor will usually put you back on your pre-pregnancy dose straight after you give birth.
Your doctor will order another blood test 4 to 8 weeks later.
Tell your doctor if you are breastfeeding.
Levothyroxine passes into breast milk.
No harmful effects on breastfed babies have been reported.
Treating hypothyroidism properly may also help milk supply if it is low.
Your dose needs may be different while you are nursing.
You may be more likely to have a broken bone while using levothyroxine.
This is particularly true if your dose is higher than you need.

It works by decreasing certain chemicals that tighten the blood vessels.
Blood flows more smoothly.
The heart can pump blood more efficiently.
High blood pressure is a common condition.
When not treated, it can cause damage to the brain, heart, blood vessels, kidneys, and other parts of the body.
Damage to these organs may cause heart disease.
It may cause a heart attack.
It may cause heart failure.
It may cause a stroke.
It may cause kidney failure.
It may cause loss of vision.
It may cause other problems.
Taking medication will help to control your blood pressure.
Making lifestyle changes will also help to control your blood pressure.
These changes include eating a diet that is low in fat and salt.

evidence_text:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to lisinopril.
Signs of an allergic reaction to lisinopril include severe stomach pain, hives, difficult breathing, and swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat.
Lisinopril may cause serious side effects.
Call your doctor at once if you have:
a light-headed feeling, like you might pass out;
high blood potassium - nausea, weakness, tingly feeling, chest pain, irregular heartbeats, loss of movement;
low white blood cell counts - fever, mouth sores, skin sores, sore throat, cough;
kidney problems - swelling, urinating less, feeling tired or short of breath; or
liver problems - loss of appetite, stomach pain (upper right side), tiredness, itching, dark urine, clay-colored stools, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or eyes).
Common lisinopril side effects may include:
headache, dizziness;
low blood pressure, cough; or
chest pain.
This is not a complete list of side effects and others may occur.
Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
You may report side effects to FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

subject: Lisinopril
relation_definition: The subject drug may cause the serious or potentially dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity that requires medical attention.
evidence_text:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to lisinopril.
Signs of an allergic reaction to lisinopril include severe stomach pain, hives, difficult breathing, and swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat.
Lisinopril may cause serious side effects.
Call your doctor at once if you have:
a light-headed feeling, like you might pass out;
high blood potassium - nausea, weakness, tingly feeling, chest pain, irregular heartbeats, loss of movement;
low white blood cell counts - fever, mouth sores, skin sores, sore throat, cough;
kidney problems - swelling, urinating less, feeling tired or short of breath; or
liver problems - loss of appetite, stomach pain (upper right side), tiredness, itching, dark urine, clay-colored stools, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or eyes).
Common lisinopril side effects may include:
headache, dizziness;
low blood pressure, cough; or
chest pain.
This is not a complete list of side effects and others may occur.
Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
You may report side effects to FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

evidence_text:
Lisinopril can harm your kidneys.
This risk is especially high if you also use certain medicines.
These medicines are for infections, cancer, or osteoporosis.
Tell your doctor about all your other medicines, especially:
a diuretic or "water pill" that may increase blood potassium such as spironolactone, triamterene, or amiloride;
NSAIDs (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs) - aspirin, ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin), naproxen (Aleve), celecoxib, diclofenac, indomethacin, meloxicam, and others;
insulin or diabetes medications;
medicine to prevent organ transplant rejection such as temsirolimus, sirolimus, or everolimus; or
heart or blood pressure medication
lithium
gold injections.
This list is not complete.
Other drugs may interact with lisinopril.
These include prescription and over-the-counter medicines.
These also include vitamins and herbal products.
Not all possible drug interactions are listed here.
